providers.evidence: Darwin close is implemented by the host bridge's coherent guest descriptor namespace: sockets dispatch through the Winsock-backed registry, filesystem descriptors are validated against the tracked guest namespace, and successful CRT close removes the descriptor from guest-visible enumeration.

Darwin effective gid is derived from the Windows effective identity token primary-group SID terminal RID. Thread impersonation is honored when present, otherwise the process token is used; query failure is fatal instead of fabricating an identity.

Darwin effective uid is derived from the Windows effective identity token user SID terminal RID. Thread impersonation is honored when present, otherwise the process token is used; query failure is fatal instead of fabricating an identity.

Darwin real gid is derived from the current Windows process token primary-group SID terminal RID, preserving a stable OS-backed 32-bit process identity and failing visibly if the token identity cannot be queried.
Darwin getpid process identity is implemented by the Windows CRT _getpid-backed Darwin host bridge and covered by the generated semantic-provider/import-router smoke tests.

Darwin real uid is derived from the current Windows process token user SID terminal RID, preserving a stable OS-backed 32-bit process identity and failing visibly if the token identity cannot be queried.

Darwin lseek uses the host bridge's 64-bit _lseeki64 implementation over the same tracked guest file-descriptor namespace, preserving signed 64-bit off_t width, SEEK_SET/SEEK_CUR/SEEK_END behavior, and CRT errno rather than truncating through Windows long.

Darwin write uses the coherent guest descriptor namespace, dispatches socket descriptors through the Winsock-backed send path, writes tracked regular-file descriptors through UCRT, preserves zero-length behavior, and validates the complete readable guest buffer span before any host API dereferences it.
